question: Does the MBCP Mindoro island-wide biodiversity report provide fish-specific, waterbody-resolved evidence suitable for Bangwit's regional freshwater baseline?

source.title: Rapid Island-Wide Survey of Terrestrial Fauna and Flora on Mindoro Island, Philippines
source.subtitle: With additional notes on the results of the fauna and flora inventory of selected priority areas for biodiversity conservation in Mindoro Oriental Province
source.rightsStatement: The report states © Mindoro Biodiversity Conservation Foundation Inc., All rights reserved. It prohibits reproduction for resale or other commercial purposes without express written permission. No open license or affirmative public-app reuse permission was found.

surveyContext.reportFocus: A conservation-oriented island-wide account of terrestrial fauna and flora, combining rapid assessment, interviews, observations, previous records, and detailed inventories of selected Oriental Mindoro sites. Fish are a small part of the narrative and map content, not the subject of a dedicated fish survey.
surveyContext.generalFieldPeriod: The report describes selected Oriental Mindoro inventories during May-August 1998 and January and October-November 1999. The fish-specific statements are not assigned to a field date or effort window.
surveyContext.methodsRelevantToInterpretation: The island-wide rapid assessment used accessible communities, local interviews, direct observations where feasible, and supplementary reports. The detailed selected-site methods emphasize terrestrial vertebrates; no fish-specific capture protocol, station list, sampling effort, voucher roster, or specimen-custody record was located.
limitations: Do not attach the report-wide 1998-1999 survey period to each fish statement as if it were a fish collection date.
The river and lake labels on the island map are not a fish station inventory or licensed waterbody geometry.

The map legend distinguishes confirmed and unconfirmed records, but the reviewed text does not provide a fish record-to-site matrix, event dates, vouchers, coordinates, or a traceable evidence basis for each marker.
The report itself says Mindoro fish knowledge was poor and that additional freshwater research was needed.

narrativeStatements.disposition: Retain as a historical waterbody research lead only; the report does not link it to a dated 1998-1999 fish event or a specimen.
Keep at genus level as an unresolved historical collection lead; do not assign a modern species name or public occurrence without the specimen and identification evidence.

narrativeStatements.reportedLocality: Naujan Lake via the Butas River estuary
narrativeStatements.disposition: Do not convert the general statement into a captured specimen, a lake-wide occurrence, or a species-level identification.

fishSourceLeads.mapDisposition: Preserved only as verbatim source labels and broad Mindoro freshwater context. Map markers were not digitized or assigned to named rivers/lakes because a source-level fish-to-marker/site crosswalk is not available in the reviewed text.

taxonomyCrosscheck.currentCatalogStatus: Valid as Barbodes hemictenus Jordan & Richardson 1908; Catalog online version updated 2026-08-13.
taxonomyCrosscheck.scope: Nomenclatural crosswalk only. It does not re-identify the report's unnamed specimen or verify a particular river, lake, collection date, or current presence. Other map labels remain verbatim and unnormalized.

decision.reason: The report is useful for identifying Mindoro inland-water follow-up sites and historical taxon leads, but fish-specific dates, effort, specimen links, site-level map crosswalks, and public-app reuse permission are missing.

nextAction: Continue MIMAROPA freshwater work with independently documented, named-waterbody fish surveys and current voucher evidence. Prioritize records that resolve Naujan tributaries, Anahawin River, or another Mindoro lake/river with methods and explicit reuse terms; keep this report's fish leads and map unprojected.

sources.supports: Full report title page and copyright notice; general methods and field period; Mindoro fish section, freshwater-fish map legend, named rivers and lakes, and survey limitations.
Current Catalog of Fishes nomenclatural status for Barbodes hemictenus and its type-locality record; no independent identification of this report's fish.
